main_text.p: uere oportet,& non cruda.Deinde sanguis pelte correptus concoqui, ac à natura uinci nequit:idcirco siue in amara & tenuem, siue in atram & craffam putrefactione dege neret,medicamento purgate euacuari nequaquam poteft. Caeterum euacuato corpore sanguinis milsione, aut medicameto cathartico,uires roborare, & uenenu propellere omnibus modis tentabimus. Quae uires reficiunt diximus esse pulueres diamargariti frigidi,diarrhodi Abbatis, & tria santali, quibus adde uel pulli gallinacei iu sculum oxalidę, aut succo limonij,aut citrij alteratum. Pofsumus item his uti per se,aut cum conferua rofarum, oxalidis, & radicis heptaphyli,quae in hoc affectu mirę sunt efficaciae,& praesertim poftrema. Propelletur etiam uenenum sumpta semidragma theriacae recentis cum uncijs duabus syrupi citrij,uel limonij,uel acetati simplicis,uel deniq; succi oxalidis, cum aquae ro farū uncijs tribus aut quatuor. Quòd si desideretur recens theriaca, eius loco suma tur ueteris scrupulus unus, aut semidragma,si febrilis calor nō urgeat. Iteretur hic potus,quàm frequentius sieri poterit. Huc accedunt,quae ante iā recensuimus,nempe

page.notes: Handwritten marks in the right margin, including the word "Theriacae" in manuscript beside "duabus", are not printed and were left out. "oxalidę" (line 13) is a doubtful reading of a letter after "oxalid"; it could be a printed ę or a stray mark, so it is not marked. Long s was normalised to s throughout, per the rules. Printing as given: "pofsumus", "milsione", "fucco" spellings kept as printed. The word "fumpta" (for "sumpta") is printed as such in the scan and is kept.
